q: How do I calculate emissions for servers in a colocation data centre using PUE?
title: Colocation server emissions with PUE
short: Multiply your servers' average IT power in kW by the hours in the year, then by the facility's annual PUE, then by the grid factor. In India: kWh x PUE x 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Ask the provider for your metered IT kWh and their measured annual PUE, not the design figure.
audience: Indian SaaS, fintech and IT firms with colocation racks

sections.h: The formula and what each part means
ol: IT energy: the kWh your racks actually draw, from the provider's metered power reports. If you only have a contracted kW, use average draw, not the breaker rating.
PUE: total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy, as defined in ISO/IEC 30134-2. It adds your share of cooling, UPS losses and lighting. Use the measured annual figure for the site.
Facility energy for your racks: IT kWh x PUE.
Emissions: facility kWh x the grid factor for where the data centre sits. For India, 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh from the CEA CO2 Baseline Database, version 21.0.

sections.h: What to request from the colocation provider
ul: Monthly metered kWh for your cage, racks or power strips, for the full reporting year.
The site's measured annual PUE, with the period it covers and whether it is a 12 month average.
Whether your power bill is already grossed up for PUE. Some providers bill facility power, not IT power; if so, do not multiply by PUE again.
Any renewable supply contracted for the site: open access, a green tariff or certificates, with quantities and periods, if you want a market-based figure.

p: If you contract and pay for metered power for your space and you treat the cage as a leased asset under your operational control, report it as Scope 2 purchased electricity. If power is bundled into a service fee and you control nothing on site, it is Scope 3: Category 1 purchased services, or Category 8 upstream leased assets if you report leased space there. Pick one treatment, write it in your method note and keep it every year.

The location-based figure uses the grid factor regardless of contracts. A market-based figure can be lower only if the provider passes you a share of renewable power backed by instruments for the same period, and you have the documents. A provider's statement that the site is green, with no quantities, does not change your market-based number.

example.title: Worked example: a 20 kW colocation footprint in Mumbai
lines: Average IT draw: 20 kW, running all year
Annual PUE from the provider: 1.6, so facility energy = 175,200 x 1.6 = 280,320 kWh
Location-based: 280,320 x 0.710 = 199,027 kg CO2, about 199 tonnes a year
If the provider documents that 40% of your share is renewable: 280,320 x 0.60 x 0.710 = 119,416 kg CO2 market-based
example.note: The 40% renewable share is an assumption for illustration; use only shares backed by certificates or contracts for the period.
